How to use Knitt.

Connect your Git project, choose a conversation, and carry its context into your next coding session.

Already ran npx @tinchu0/knitt@next setup and completed the prompts? Your project is connected. You don’t need to build a package or install it again.

Open your connected project.

Restart the coding agents you selected during setup, open the Git project you connected, and approve their normal MCP and hook trust prompts.

If you only downloaded Knitt without completing setup, or want to connect another project, run:

npx @tinchu0/knitt@next setup

Choose the project and clients in the prompts. Once setup finishes, continue below.

Choose a chat. Pick up the thread.

In a fresh session in the connected project, run:

/continue-chat

If slash skills aren’t available, ask your agent:

Use Knitt’s shared-memory connection to open the conversation picker. Let me choose a chat, then retrieve its checkpoint and summarize the last progress and next step.

The picker currently discovers local Antigravity conversations for this repository and its linked worktrees. Choose one, review the restored checkpoint, then give your agent a concrete next step. Choose again in each new session.

Continue the retry implementation from this checkpoint. Inspect the current branch first and run the relevant tests after making changes.

Need an earlier detail? Ask the agent to search the selected conversation and retrieve the original evidence with search_memory and get_evidence.

Keep your progress.

Supported coding-client hooks capture available conversation text after selection, when trusted and executed. You can also ask for an explicit checkpoint:

Use save_memory to record the goal, decisions and their reasons, files changed, actual test results, blockers, and next step for this selected conversation.

Ordinary chat clients require explicit saves. Checkpoints are reference material: inspect current files and branch state before acting. Raw tool results, images, and hidden reasoning are excluded. Credential redaction is best effort; keep secrets out of saved text.

Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, and Claude web

For Claude Desktop, include --client claude-desktop during setup, then manually merge the project’s .memory/connectors/claude-desktop.json mcpServers entry into Desktop’s MCP settings and restart it.

In an ordinary chat, ask the agent to call start_session, then choose_conversation, wait for your selection, and call get_context. Use the returned session ID and ask for save_memory after progress.

ChatGPT and Claude web require a separately hosted HTTPS MCP endpoint and compatible OAuth provider. Local setup does not deploy or connect that service. Local memory stays on one machine; team sharing needs a shared authenticated service.

Check, update, roll back, or disconnect

Inspect your installation:

npx @tinchu0/knitt@next doctor

configured confirms local paths and managed settings, not client login, trust, or a live handoff. Use the same custom --home path throughout if you configured one.

Update your installed runtime:

npx @tinchu0/knitt@next update --yes

Roll back if a previous runtime exists, or disconnect a project:

npx @tinchu0/knitt@next rollback --yes

npx @tinchu0/knitt@next uninstall \
  --workspace /absolute/path/to/your-project --yes

Uninstall restores unchanged managed settings and retains user edits, runtime, and memory. Remove any manually merged Desktop entry yourself.

Troubleshooting
  • No tools or slash skill? Restart the client in the connected project, check MCP and hook trust prompts, and run doctor.
  • Empty picker? Check for a local Antigravity conversation associated with this repository or its worktrees. Other account histories are not imported.
  • No chat selected or wrong repository? Open the intended project and choose its conversation in the current session.
  • Missing session ID? Reload the connection and start a fresh session. Ordinary chats must use start_session; don’t invent an ID.
  • Configuration conflict? Review the named file. Legacy or manually edited settings are not automatically overwritten.
  • Changed Node installation? Rerun setup to refresh absolute executable paths.
  • Recent work missing? Check selection, hook trust and execution, or whether an explicit save succeeded.
